chunks: When they despaired of (persuading) him, they went aside to confer. The oldest of them said: "You know that your father has pledged you in the name of God, and you have been guilty of iniquity in the case of Joseph before. I will not leave this place unless my father permits or God decides for me, for He is the best of all judges."
ai.seo_question: What did the eldest brother say to his siblings when they conferred privately about their father's pledge?
ai.summary: In this verse, the eldest brother, often identified in Shia exegesis as Reuben (Rubil), serves as the moral authority, reminding his siblings of the *mawthiq* (solemn covenant) with Jacob and their prior negligence toward Joseph. His declaration that he will not leave until his father permits or God decrees highlights the interplay between paternal authority and divine will (*Hakim*), a key theme in Shia understanding of familial piety and patience during trials.
